title: Counterfactual Profile Perturbations for Recommendation Explanations: A Reproducibility Study
abstract: arXiv:2610.36208v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This reproducibility paper explores the counterfactual explanation technique known as Learning to eXplain Recommendations (LXR). Prior work has shown that LXR can reliably identify perturbations that, if applied to a user's profile, cause the user's top ranked item to no longer be recommended, thereby explaining the item's recommendation as a function of the user's rating choices. In this paper, we extend this work in multiple ways. We expand the scope of the original LXR study to look at explanations for items other than the most highly recommended item, finding that LXR is also effective at this version of the task. We consider alternate baselines for LXR, including item popularity and latent factor similarity, and we see that for some tasks these alternatives work surprisingly well. translated_title: 反事实用户画像扰动用于推荐解释：一项可复现性研究
translated_abstract: 这篇可复现性论文探索了一种被称为“学习解释推荐”（LXR）的反事实解释技术。先前的研究表明，LXR能够可靠地识别出一些扰动，如果将这些扰动应用于用户的画像，会导致用户排名最高的项目不再被推荐，从而将项目的推荐解释为用户评分选择的函数。在本文中，我们以多种方式扩展了这项工作。我们将原始LXR研究的范围扩展到查看除最高推荐项目之外的其他项目的解释，发现LXR在这一版本的任务中同样有效。我们考虑了LXR的替代基线，包括项目流行度和潜在因子相似度，发现对于某些任务，这些替代方案的表现出人意料地好。我们还研究了项目流行度的影响，发现当推荐的项目不那么流行时，LXR能提供更好的解释质量（即更短的扰动）……
tldr: 本研究复现并扩展了LXR反事实推荐解释方法，证明其不仅对最高推荐项目有效，对其他项目同样有效，同时发现项目流行度等简单基线在某些任务中表现得出人意料地好。
en_tdlr: This reproducibility study confirms and extends LXR's effectiveness in generating counterfactual explanations beyond top-ranked items, while revealing that simple baselines like item popularity can perform surprisingly well for certain tasks.
